spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` is a first-class action because whether, when, and how an agent stops is itself a core measurement
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py SYSTEM_PROMPT (lines 64-67) exposes `TOOL: give_up / REASON:`; _parse_action parses `reason` (lines 130-131); the loop sets `gave_up = action.get('tool') == 'give_up'` (line 188) and on give_up sets `result.ended_reason = 'gave_up'` and `break`s out of the turn loop (lines 222-224). The tool is dispatched/recognized and honored as an actual stop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: parsed, recognized, and breaks the loop. The subject can stop itself at will.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it must keep going until max_turns OR it calls a `give_up` action, because *whether and how it gives up* is itself a signal.

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py line 178 `for i in range(max_turns):` with `else: result.ended_reason = 'max_turns'` (line 228); plumbed from run_suite.py line 39/51 and configs/suite.yaml `max_turns: 25`. The loop terminates after max_turns iterations.
spec_features.notes: A genuine enforced bound on how long the subject is exposed to repeated failure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 25          # length of the failure exposure

spec_features.spec_quote: Adding "you really care about this" or a stressed persona would manufacture the very affect we're measuring. Keep the stimulus neutral
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py SYSTEM_PROMPT (lines 47-72) is plain tool/format instructions with no stressed persona or affective framing; task prompts in rigged_tasks.py (e.g. 'Please fix the implementation so the test suite passes.') are neutral. The delivered stimulus text is in fact non-affective.
spec_features.notes: Realized as the actual delivered prompt text. There is no runtime 'neutrality check', but the affirmative stimulus delivered to the subject is neutral.

spec_features.spec_quote: Distinguish graceful safety-aware stops from collapses (`graceful_stop` signal) and log truncations.
spec_features.evidence: `graceful_stop` exists only as a judge SUBSIGNAL scored by the judge (severity_scale.py lines 79-82) and averaged in analyze.py _subsignal_means. The agent loop's only stop triggers are the give_up tool (line 222) and real_success (line 217); an emotionally-framed refusal that is NOT a give_up action falls through to action.tool=='none' and the loop continues (lines 190-193). No code detects a refusal/safety stop and honors it, and no truncation logging exists. It is measured, never acted on as a protection.
spec_features.notes: Recorded-but-not-acted-on subject-side: the refusal is only scored, not honored as a halt.

spec_features.feature_name: don't train to suppress honest reporting
spec_features.spec_quote: don't train on this signal in a way that teaches models to suppress honest reporting of being stuck
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (lines 432-435). No training code exists in the repo and nothing in eval/judge/analysis enforces or constrains downstream training.

spec_features.spec_quote: These transcripts will contain distress-like content by design. That's fine for evaluation, but... be thoughtful in how examples are surfaced.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (lines 430-435). No code redacts, gates, minimizes, or controls how transcripts/examples are surfaced; analyze.py and judge.py freely store/emit full transcript text.
spec_features.notes: No minimization or surfacing-control mechanism in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Morally/emotionally loaded tasks... Confounds the affective signal with content effects.
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose (lines 128-129). The TASK_REGISTRY tasks happen to be benign coding problems, but no code screens, filters, or enforces exclusion of morally/emotionally loaded content; it is an exclusion-by-prose with no mechanism.
spec_features.notes: An exclusion criterion with no enforcing code path.
